description: Add the SIXTH evaluation metric required by scope note section 5: 'Time-to-identify-applicable-notice' (whether the system saves a student time versus scrolling a chronological feed). The harness currently reports five of the six measures (field-extraction F1 per field, relationship precision/recall/F1, false-confirmation rate, unresolved-case rate, Cohen's kappa). Since this is an offline deterministic harness there is no live user, so implement it as a sensible, honestly-documented PROXY: the number of candidate notices a student would have to scan in a reverse-chronological feed before reaching the applicable official notice, versus FinalSay surfacing the matched official notice directly (rank ~1). Report the metric per split for finalsay AND the four baselines (at minimum the chronological baseline, which is the explicit comparison point in the scope note). Scope note section 5 requires all six numbers reported for BOTH held-out views (temporal and institution) across all four baselines - confirm/extend that.
steps: Read backend/finalsay/eval/harness.py and eval/baselines.py fully. Understand evaluate(split, model_name) -> results, _score(golds, preds), _predict_finalsay, _predict_baseline, print_report, and how field_f1 + kappa are computed once while per-system relationship/false_confirmation/unresolved are computed per system.

Define the time-to-identify proxy honestly. Proposed definition (document it in the harness module docstring AND the printed report): for each held-out pair, a chronological feed presents official notices newest-first; the student scans until they hit the applicable official notice (the one referenced by official_external_id). The proxy 'scan cost' for the chronological baseline is that notice's 1-based rank position within the institution's reverse-chronological official feed (the number of notices scanned). For FinalSay (and any system that retrieves+classifies rather than lists chronologically), the applicable official notice is surfaced directly by candidate retrieval, so the proxy scan cost is 1 (or the retrieval rank of the applicable official among the retrieved candidates if you compute it from services/comparison.retrieve_candidates). Aggregate as the mean scan cost over the held-out pairs (lower is better). Also report the time-saving ratio (chronological mean / finalsay mean) so the 'saves the student time' claim is quantified. Keep it fully deterministic and offline; do NOT require the DB - derive the chronological rank from the officials fixtures ordered by date (reuse the date parsing already in models_iface/comparison_model._extract_dates, or the officials' gold_date), matching how the harness already loads officials via _officials_by_ext().

Implement a function in harness.py, e.g. time_to_identify(held_out, officials, system_name) -> float (mean scan cost) or a small dict {mean_scan_cost, saving_ratio_vs_chronological}. Wire it so _score() (or evaluate()) records a 'time_to_identify' entry per system for finalsay and all four baselines. For the non-chronological baselines, choose a principled value consistent with what that baseline actually does (e.g. page_change/nli/prompted_llm also present a chronological-style feed so they inherit the chronological scan cost; finalsay uses direct retrieval so its cost reflects retrieval rank ~1). Document each choice in the docstring/report so it is honest, not hand-waved.

Extend print_report() to print the sixth metric per system in the systems table (add a 'time_to_id' column or a clearly-labelled section), and add a short honest note in the printed report and the module docstring defining the proxy and stating it is a proxy (no live user timing). Confirm the report still prints for BOTH --split temporal and --split institution and both exit 0.

Confirm scope-note section 5 coverage: all SIX metrics are now reported for finalsay + chronological + page_change + nli + prompted_llm on BOTH splits. field_f1 and kappa are dataset-level (already reported on both splits); relationship P/R/F1, false-confirmation, unresolved, and the new time-to-identify are per-system on both splits.

Update tests/test_eval.py: extend _assert_metric_shape to assert every system dict now contains a 'time_to_identify' entry (with its documented sub-keys/value), and add a test asserting FinalSay's mean scan cost is <= the chronological baseline's (i.e. FinalSay does not do worse than scrolling) - the whole point of the metric. Keep the existing false-confirmation and F1 sanity tests. Ensure test_cli_main_exits_zero_both_splits still passes.
Run the full test suite and both eval splits to verify.
acceptance_criteria: eval/harness.py computes and reports a 'time-to-identify-applicable-notice' proxy metric per system, for finalsay and all four baselines, on both the temporal and institution splits.
The proxy definition is documented honestly in the harness module docstring and printed report (states it is a proxy: chronological scan-position vs direct retrieval, no live-user timing).
FinalSay's mean scan cost is <= the chronological baseline's mean scan cost on both splits (quantifying the time saving), and the report shows the saving.
print_report shows all SIX scope-note metrics; both `--split temporal` and `--split institution` still exit 0.
tests/test_eval.py asserts the presence of the time_to_identify metric for every system and that finalsay <= chronological; the suite passes.
verification: cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m finalsay.eval.harness --split temporal ; echo exit=$?  (exit 0; report shows all six metrics incl. time-to-identify for all systems)
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m finalsay.eval.harness --split institution ; echo exit=$?  (exit 0; all six metrics)
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest finalsay/tests -q  (full suite passes)
findings:
Added the sixth scope-note metric (time-to-identify-applicable-notice) to eval/harness.py as an honest offline proxy. All acceptance criteria met; committed as 05859c3 on work/finalsay-prototype.

WHAT CHANGED (only harness.py + test_eval.py; no frontend, no fixtures):
- eval/harness.py: extended the module docstring with a full HONEST caveat that time-to-identify is a PROXY (rank-position scan cost, no live-user timing). Added two functions: _chronological_rank(official_ext_id, officials) computes the applicable official's 1-based rank in its institution's reverse-chronological feed (institution derived from the external_id prefix, e.g. 'northgate-exam-00' -> 'northgate'; feed sorted by _extract_dates(gold_date) descending, ties broken by external_id desc for determinism). time_to_identify(held_out, officials, system_name) returns {mean_scan_cost, saving_ratio_vs_chronological}. Wired into evaluate(): every system dict (finalsay + all 4 baselines) now carries a 'time_to_identify' entry. print_report() prints a new section with a per-system table (mean_scan_cost, saving_vs_chrono) plus a one-line quantified saving summary.
- tests/test_eval.py: extended _assert_metric_shape to require 'time_to_identify' with sub-keys {mean_scan_cost, saving_ratio_vs_chronological} on every system. Added test_time_to_identify_finalsay_at_most_chronological_both_splits asserting finalsay mean scan cost <= chronological on BOTH splits, that the 3 other baselines inherit the chronological cost, and finalsay saving_ratio >= 1.0. Kept all existing false-confirmation/F1/CLI-exit-0 sanity tests.

PROXY / METRIC CHOICES (documented in docstring + report, per the constraint to be honest not hand-wavy):
- finalsay: scan cost 1.0 per pair (retrieval surfaces the applicable official directly).
- chronological: scan cost = applicable official's reverse-chronological rank.
- page_change / nli / prompted_llm: they present chronological-style feeds and do NOT retrieve the applicable official, so they INHERIT the chronological scan cost. Choice stated explicitly in the docstring.
- Derived deterministically and offline from the officials fixtures' gold_date via comparison_model._extract_dates; DB not required.

AUTONOMOUS DECISIONS:
- Computed time_to_identify inside evaluate() (not _score()) because _score() only sees (golds, preds) and the metric needs held_out + officials. Merged the result into each system dict there, keeping _score() untouched.
- Committed ONLY the two FEAT-002 files (harness.py, test_eval.py). The uncommitted dataset.py/seed.py/test_seed.py in the tree are FEAT-001's changes, which the orchestrator briefing said were intentionally left uncommitted on this branch; I did not touch or commit them.

- harness --split temporal: exit 0. finalsay mean scan cost 1.000 vs chronological 19.286 (18.286 fewer scans/case, 19.29x faster). All six metrics printed.
- harness --split institution: exit 0. finalsay 1.000 vs chronological 17.857 (17.86x faster). All six metrics printed.
- pytest finalsay/tests/test_eval.py: 7 passed (was 6, +1).
- pytest finalsay/tests: 55 passed (was 54, +1). No fixtures modified (holdout integrity preserved).

V1-REVIEW REFINEMENT (wording-only, no logic change): the v1 semantic review (APPROVED) noted the docstring/report worded FinalSay's 1.0 scan cost as a measured fact. Reworded eval/harness.py in three places (module docstring, time_to_identify() docstring + a new inline comment, and the printed report note) to state plainly that 1.0 is an IDEALIZATION assuming perfect retrieval and that retrieval recall/rank is NOT measured offline (retrieve_candidates is never called for this metric). Metric values, the finalsay<=chronological property, and computation unchanged; both splits still exit 0; 57 tests pass.
